title: This 4-Inch Bug Eats Turtles, Snakes and Ducklings

scenes.text: This bug eats turtles. And snakes. And ducklings.
The giant water bug. The biggest ones grow past four inches, the length of a baseball card.
It hangs on an underwater plant, dead still, and grabs whatever swims past with its front legs.
Then a dagger of a mouth goes in. It injects enzymes that turn the insides to soup, and drinks them. Big meals take hours.
In 2011 a scientist in Japan watched one catch a turtle. Others take venomous snakes, prey ten times their own size.
Then the strangest part. The male carries the eggs on his back until every one hatches. Killer. Also dad.

description:
Giant water bugs have been recorded eating turtles, venomous snakes, ducklings and fish, prey up to ten times their own size.
The largest species pass four inches. The bug ambushes from underwater plants, injects enzymes through a dagger-like proboscis and sucks out the liquefied insides, a meal that can take hours. In 2011 Japanese entomologist Shin-ya Ohba recorded the first giant water bug preying on a turtle, and in many species the male carries the eggs on his back until they hatch.
Would you swim in a pond that had these in it?
subject: giant water bug
first_comment: About 150 species of giant water bug are known, and the nymphs start on tadpoles and small fish before they graduate to turtles. What is the scariest insect you have ever met?
